dataset_info.title: Advanced Technologies & Materials Dataset
dataset_info.description: Structured catalog of advanced/emerging technologies, advanced materials, and advanced wearable suits, including properties, categories, applications, and readiness levels.

fields.name: item name
fields.readiness_level: TRL 1-9 (Technology Readiness Level) or commercial status

items.name: Quantum Computing
items.description: Computation using qubits that leverage superposition and entanglement to solve certain problems exponentially faster than classical computers.

items.name: Holographic Display Systems
items.description: Systems that project or render true 3D light-field images viewable without headsets, using techniques like diffraction, light-field arrays, or plasma excitation.

items.name: Neuromorphic Computing
items.description: Chip architectures that mimic biological neural structures for highly efficient, event-driven processing.

properties.power_efficiency: orders of magnitude better than von Neumann architecture for specific tasks

items.name: Additive Manufacturing (Metal 3D Printing)
items.description: Layer-by-layer fabrication of metal parts using techniques like powder bed fusion or directed energy deposition.

items.name: Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI)
items.description: Direct communication pathways between neural activity and external devices, invasive or non-invasive.

items.name: Fusion Energy (Magnetic/Inertial Confinement)
items.description: Energy generation via nuclear fusion reactions, using tokamak, stellarator, or laser-based inertial confinement approaches.

items.name: Graphene
items.description: Single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, exhibiting exceptional strength and conductivity.

items.name: Metamaterials
items.description: Artificially structured materials engineered to have properties not found in nature, such as negative refractive index.

items.name: Aerogel
items.description: Ultra-low-density synthetic porous material derived from a gel, with the liquid replaced by gas.

items.name: Shape Memory Alloys (e.g., Nitinol)
items.description: Alloys that can return to a predetermined shape when heated, due to a phase transformation.

items.name: High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs)
items.description: Alloys composed of five or more principal elements in near-equal proportions, offering unusual strength and corrosion resistance.

items.name: Perovskite Solar Cell Material
items.description: Crystal-structured compounds used as light-harvesting layers in next-generation solar cells, offering high efficiency at low cost.

items.name: Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP)
items.description: Composite material combining carbon fiber strands with polymer resin, offering high strength-to-weight ratio.

items.name: Topological Insulators
items.description: Materials that are insulating in the bulk but conduct electricity on their surface via protected quantum states.

items.name: Photonic Computing
items.description: Computation using photons instead of electrons for data transfer and processing, enabling higher bandwidth and lower heat generation.

properties.medium: light/photons via waveguides or free-space optics
properties.advantage: near-light-speed signal transfer, reduced resistive heating

items.name: Directed Energy Weapons Systems
items.description: Systems that use focused energy (lasers, microwaves, particle beams) for precision effects, primarily developed for defense applications.

items.name: Swarm Robotics
items.description: Coordinated systems of many simple robots that exhibit complex collective behavior through local interactions, inspired by insect colonies.

properties.scalability: designed for hundreds to thousands of units

items.name: Digital Twin Simulation
items.description: Virtual, continuously updated replicas of physical systems used for real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization.

items.name: Self-Healing Polymers
items.description: Polymeric materials engineered to autonomously repair physical damage through embedded microcapsules, reversible bonds, or vascular networks.

properties.recovery: can restore up to 90%+ of original strength

items.name: MXenes
items.description: Family of 2D transition metal carbides/nitrides known for high conductivity and tunable surface chemistry.

items.name: Ultra-High-Temperature Ceramics (UHTCs)
items.description: Ceramic compounds (e.g., hafnium carbide, zirconium diboride) that retain structural integrity at extreme temperatures above 2000°C.

items.name: Powered Exoskeleton Suit
items.description: Wearable robotic frame with motorized joints that augments human strength and endurance for industrial, military, or medical use.

properties.load_augmentation: can add 20-90+ kg of effective lift capacity

items.name: Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Space Suit
items.description: Pressurized, life-supporting suit designed for survival and mobility in the vacuum of space, incorporating thermal regulation and micrometeoroid protection.

properties.layers: multi-layer insulation, pressure bladder, micrometeoroid garment
properties.life_support: self-contained oxygen, CO2 scrubbing, thermal control

items.name: Smart Textile / E-Textile Suit
items.description: Clothing embedded with conductive fibers, sensors, and flexible electronics for biometric monitoring and adaptive functions.

properties.components: conductive thread, flexible sensors, embedded microelectronics

items.name: Advanced Hazmat / CBRN Protective Suit
items.description: Fully encapsulating protective suit engineered to shield against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear hazards.

properties.materials: laminated barrier films, activated carbon layers
properties.protection_level: rated by permeation resistance standards (e.g., NFPA 1991)

items.name: Liquid Cooling/Warming Garment (LCVG)
items.description: Undergarment with embedded tubing circulating temperature-controlled fluid to regulate body temperature in extreme environments or under a sealed suit.

properties.mechanism: network of thin tubes carrying water for active thermal exchange
properties.use_context: worn beneath EVA suits or firefighting gear

items.name: Soft Robotic Assistive Suit
items.description: Lightweight, fabric-based wearable using pneumatic or cable-driven actuators to assist natural movement without rigid frames.

properties.actuation: pneumatic bladders or Bowden cable systems

items.name: Solid-State Batteries
items.description: Battery technology using solid electrolytes instead of liquid, offering higher energy density and improved safety over lithium-ion.

properties.safety: reduced fire risk (no flammable liquid electrolyte)

items.name: CRISPR Gene Editing
items.description: Precision gene-editing technology using guide RNA and Cas enzymes to target and modify specific DNA sequences.

properties.precision: single base-pair editing possible (with newer variants)

items.name: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs)
items.description: Untethered robotic vehicles that operate underwater without real-time human control, using onboard navigation and sensing.

properties.navigation: inertial navigation, sonar, occasionally GPS surfacing
properties.endurance: hours to months depending on design (gliders)

items.name: Space-Based Solar Power
items.description: Concept and emerging systems for collecting solar energy in orbit and transmitting it wirelessly to Earth via microwave or laser beams.

properties.collection: orbital solar arrays, unaffected by weather/night
properties.transmission: microwave or laser beaming to ground rectenna

items.name: Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs)
items.description: Cylindrical nanostructures of rolled graphene sheets, exhibiting exceptional tensile strength and electrical conductivity.

properties.electrical_conductivity: can be metallic or semiconducting depending on chirality

items.name: Metallic Glass (Amorphous Metal)
items.description: Metal alloys with a disordered, non-crystalline atomic structure, giving high strength and elasticity with resistance to wear.

items.name: Programmable/4D-Printed Materials
items.description: Materials designed to change shape or properties over time or in response to stimuli after 3D printing, adding a 'time' dimension to fabrication.

properties.mechanism: engineered material anisotropy and composite layering

items.name: Diving/Atmospheric Diving Suit (ADS)
items.description: Rigid, articulated pressure suit that maintains one atmosphere of internal pressure, allowing divers to work at extreme depths without decompression.

items.name: Firefighter Proximity/Fire-Entry Suit
items.description: Reflective, heat-resistant suit designed to allow close-range work near extreme heat sources such as aircraft fires or industrial furnaces.

properties.materials: aluminized outer layer over fire-resistant composite insulation
properties.heat_resistance: withstands radiant heat up to ~1000°C briefly

items.name: Camouflage / Adaptive Optical Suit
items.description: Experimental wearable systems using electrochromic materials or camera-projector arrays to dynamically match surroundings for concealment.

items.name: Integrated Powered Armor Concept (HUD + Repulsor-style Propulsion)
items.description: Speculative full-body powered armor concept combining structural exoskeleton, heads-up-display (HUD) visor, and distributed thrust modules for flight — inspired by fictional powered-armor designs (e.g., Iron Man). Not an existing deployed system; included as a conceptual/aspirational entry blending real sub-technologies.

properties.status: conceptual - no unified system exists; individual components exist separately at varying TRLs
properties.power_challenge: no current compact power source matches fictional portrayals (arc-reactor-equivalent energy density does not exist)

applications: component technologies used separately in real jet suits, HUD helmets, exoskeletons

items.name: Jet Suit (Real Personal Flight System)
items.description: Real, commercially demonstrated wearable propulsion system using micro-turbine engines mounted on arms and back to enable controlled personal flight.

properties.flight_time: roughly 5-10 minutes per fuel load (current generation)
properties.top_speed: demonstrated over 30 mph in public trials

items.name: Augmented-Reality HUD Helmet
items.description: Helmet-integrated visor projecting real-time data, navigation, targeting, or diagnostic overlays into the wearer's field of view.

items.name: Wearable Exosuit with AI Load-Balancing (Iron-Man-style Assist Concept)
items.description: Speculative near-future extension of current exoskeletons: an AI-driven suit that predicts user intent and dynamically redistributes load across actuators in real time, echoing fictional 'smart armor' concepts.

properties.ai_role: predictive intent modeling from EMG/motion sensors to preemptively adjust actuator torque
properties.status: research-stage; predictive-assist exosuits exist, full 'smart armor' integration does not
